svg.aria-label: The periodic table: its structure and the elements most used in rebuilding. The elements are arranged in order of atomic number (number of protons); the rows are periods, 7 in all, and an atom in period n has n electron shells; the columns are groups, 18 in all, and the last digit of a main-group number equals the number of outer electrons. Metals lie in the lower left and middle and are the great majority; non-metals lie in the upper right; along the staircase line between them are the metalloids (boron, silicon, germanium, arsenic, antimony, tellurium), many of them semiconductors; the far right column is the noble gases, which hardly take part in chemical reactions; the lanthanides and actinides are placed separately below the table. Across a period from left to right, atoms get smaller, metallic character weakens and non-metallic character strengthens; down a group, atoms get larger, metals get more reactive and non-metals less reactive. The elements most used in rebuilding and their main uses: hydrogen, fuel, chemical industry; carbon, fuel, reducing agent for iron, a component of steel; nitrogen, fertiliser; oxygen, burning, breathing; sodium, salt, soda ash, caustic soda, soap; magnesium, light alloys, fire-starting; aluminium, casting, utensils; silicon, glass, cement, ceramics; phosphorus, fertiliser; sulphur, sulphuric acid, vulcanising rubber, killing germs; chlorine, disinfectants; potassium, fertiliser, alkali, soap; calcium, lime, cement, improving soil; iron, tools, machines, building; copper, wire, bronze, brass; zinc, brass, galvanising, batteries; tin, bronze, solder, tin plating; lead, solder, weights, shielding; silver, solder, contacts, mirrors; gold, contacts, exchange; iodine, iodised salt, tincture of iodine for disinfection; tungsten, cutting tools, lamp filaments; chromium and nickel, corrosion-resistant materials; mercury, highly toxic, avoid using it; arsenic, highly toxic, do not use

g.text: The periodic table: structure and the elements most used in rebuilding
Ordered by atomic number (number of protons); rows are periods (7 in all), columns are groups (18 in all)
Staircase line: metals lower left and middle (the
great majority), non-metals upper right; along the
line, metalloids, many of them semiconductors
Far right column: noble gases, hardly react at all
The lanthanides (57-71) and actinides (89-103) belong in column 3 of periods 6 and 7; they are too long,
so they are placed separately below the table (omitted here)
How to read the periodic table
Across a period, left to right: atoms get smaller; less metallic, more non-metallic
e.g. Na (a very reactive metal) → Mg → Al → Si → P → S → Cl (a very reactive non-metal)
Down a group: atoms get larger; metals more reactive, non-metals less reactive
e.g. Li < Na < K < Rb < Cs; F > Cl > Br > I
